claim: Human AGA evidence supports separating preserved hair-follicle stem-cell populations from a reduced progenitor-cell state; P is therefore retained as a distinct latent candidate rather than collapsed into N or R.

witnesses.source: Garza et al. 2011; PMID 21206086; PMCID PMC3026732
witnesses.assay_family: flow cytometry + localization + qPCR + functional characterization
witnesses.human_comparison: bald vs non-bald scalp from men with AGA
reported_pattern: KRT15-high stem-cell population maintained in bald scalp
LGR5 expression reduced while KRT15 was maintained

witnesses.design: 40 subjects: 14 male AGA, 6 FPHL, 20 matched controls
reported_pattern: CD34 detected in all control biopsies vs 60% of frontal bald AGA samples
CD34 staining lower in frontal bald vs hairy occipital tissue within AGA patients
Sox9 expression preserved across frontal bald, occipital hairy and control samples

projection.supported_separation: preserved stem-cell markers can coexist with reduced progenitor markers
not_supported: P is a validated scalar biomarker
the observed cross-sectional difference proves causal conversion failure

evidence_topology.remaining_common_mode: both studies infer cell-state identity through marker biology and remain cross-sectional

open_defeaters: marker expression is not identical to functional regenerative reserve
different sampling, disease stage and assay thresholds can affect apparent cell-population abundance
causal stem-to-progenitor transition failure is plausible but not longitudinally demonstrated in human scalp

next_information_gain.preferred: functional or intervention-linked progenitor assay measured before later follicle output
next_information_gain.reason: move from cell-state separation to dynamic conversion competence
